one_liner: Header-only C++11 serializer for STL/user types; faster and smaller than Boost.Serialization, no schema needed.
what_it_does: HPS serializes STL containers and user-defined types to a compact binary format directly, via header-only C++ templates; you call hps::to_string/from_string or to_stream/from_stream on your data with no IDL and no code-generation step, unlike Protobuf or Cap'n Proto. Custom types add serialize()/parse() template methods (buf << members / buf >> members) instead of adopting Boost's archive/operator<< with BOOST_SERIALIZATION macros, so it is not drop-in for Boost's API but needs much less boilerplate (README's own SLOC table: 7 vs 13 lines for a double array, 16 vs 20 for a sparse matrix).
how_it_is_fast: Signed integers are zigzag-encoded and routed through a varint-style unsigned-integer serializer (confirmed in src/basic_type/int_serializer.h), the same base idea Protobuf uses. The key difference from Protobuf is that HPS emits no field numbers or wire-type tags at all -- layout comes entirely from the C++ type at compile time (per-README) -- which cuts both encoded size and per-field dispatch overhead. It also skips the reflection/schema layer and message-builder allocation model that Cap'n Proto and Boost.Serialization pay for.
when_to_use: Serializing STL containers (vector, map, unordered_map, set, deque, list, pair, unique_ptr, string, array) or composed user types within one C++ codebase/toolchain
Want a smaller, faster wire format than Boost.Serialization without adopting an IDL or build-time codegen step (Protobuf/Cap'n Proto)
OK vendoring a small header-only C++11 library with no runtime shared-lib dependency
Numeric-heavy workloads (large arrays of primitives) similar to the library's own stated use case (quantum-chemistry data checkpointing)
Internal format where both reader and writer compile from the same C++ headers, so no cross-language schema is needed
when_not_to_use: Need cross-language interop or generated bindings (Python/Java/Go) -- there is no .proto/.capnp equivalent
Need zero-copy / read-without-parsing access into the buffer -- HPS parses into an object like Boost does; Cap'n Proto's own README-cited benchmark beats HPS specifically on the sparse-matrix case
Need forward/backward wire compatibility as fields are added or removed -- there are no field tags, so there is no story for schema evolution (unlike Protobuf's optional fields)
Project has been unmaintained since last commit 2022-01-17 with no recent validation against current compilers/Boost/Protobuf/Cap'n Proto versions
Care about stream-based reads specifically: an unresolved open issue (#49) reports an abort() in StreamInputBuffer::load on a size mismatch, with no maintainer response

integration.dependencies: none at runtime (STL only); googletest is a test-only submodule, not a runtime dependency
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (CI matrix tested GCC 5/6/7 and Clang 4.0/5.0 on Ubuntu Trusty via .travis.yml)
integration.platforms: not documented beyond Linux CI; no architecture-specific code observed in the serializers read (no SIMD/intrinsics)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial -- explain: same job (binary serialize/parse of STL + user types) as Boost.Serialization, but a different call surface (free functions hps::to_string/from_string/to_stream/from_stream vs Boost's archive objects and BOOST_SERIALIZATION_* macros); user types need new serialize()/parse() methods rather than Boost's serialize(Archive&, unsigned version)

gotchas: Open, unresolved issue #49: a third-party project hit abort() in StreamInputBuffer::load on a read-position/file-size mismatch (oldpos 524288 vs size 589548); no fix visible in the thread
No field numbers or wire types in the encoding -- reading with a mismatched type layout is undefined, unlike Protobuf's tag-based tolerance
unordered_map/unordered_set serialize in iteration order, which is not guaranteed stable across runs or STL implementations
Repo dormant since Jan 2022; last verified against 2017-era GCC 5-7 / Clang 4-5, so building with a modern compiler is unverified
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among the catalogued siblings, Cap'n Proto and zpp::bits are the closest (also binary serialization, not JSON-text parsers like the rest). Pick HPS over them when you're already on Boost.Serialization and want a smaller/faster same-shape replacement without adopting an IDL, schema compiler, or zero-copy buffer model -- but Cap'n Proto's own benchmark beats HPS on nested/sparse-matrix data and gives you cross-language schemas plus zero-copy reads that HPS doesn't offer.
verified_claims_summary: On GCC 7.2 -O3 (CentOS 7.2, Intel Xeon E5-2620 v4), HPS's own first-party benchmark (src/benchmark, run via benchmark.mk/ci.sh) times full serialize+parse round-trips against Boost 1.66.0, Protobuf 3.5.1, and Cap'n Proto 0.6.1 on a double array, sparse matrix, and string-to-double hash map; the README charts show HPS beating Boost on all three (up to ~2.5x, i.e. '150% faster', and up to 40% smaller output on several cases), while Cap'n Proto is faster than HPS specifically on the sparse-matrix case.
status_note: Abandoned: last commit 2022-01-17 and CI last green against 2017-era GCC 5-7/Clang 4-5 on Travis; MIT-licensed, header-only, and small enough to vendor and re-verify against a current compiler yourself.
